comparator.name: Middle Eastern Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations define one 180-EC Middle Eastern Studies programme, with 60 EC in each year. The complete curriculum is reproduced below at its regulated component-credit level. The two faculty-wide modules preserve their regulated choice between Global Change and Cultural Heritage, and the 30-EC minor remains genuine open minor space. No formal route is defined. The current programme page describes the 30-EC Cairo or Rabat period as the standard recommended study-abroad pathway and notes that exceptional deviation is possible; it is therefore preserved as the published curriculum component without overstating that no exception can exist.

alternatives.label: Global history, politics & Middle East–Europe relations
alternatives.labelReason: Modern history, empire, comparative politics, international relations, public international law, conflict, migration, media and European institutions form the programme’s supported spine; the label identifies a global/comparative route and does not claim regional-language or area-studies equivalence.
alternatives.concept: Study modern history, empire and colonialism, comparative politics, international relations, public international law, Europe, migration, conflict, civil society and public representation. A Mediterranean art-history course gives one concrete encounter with exchange involving Islamic courts. This is a global and comparative related-fields route, not a Middle Eastern Studies degree: it has no Arabic, region-specific history/politics sequence, Islam/Judaism core or regional immersion.
progression: Law, modern-history and comparative-politics foundations precede public international law, international relations, imperial history, sociology, conflict and advanced historical research. GOSGATE102 precedes GOSLAWJ212; introductory analytical and social-science work precedes advanced communication, media and civil-society study. Every exact planned term passes, PPD is in Year 1 and nine courses are at level 300.

alternatives.label: Culture, migration & public representation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is led by cultural encounter, empire and migration, archaeology and heritage, literature, rhetoric, media, museums and qualitative social inquiry; it does not represent those global fields as Middle Eastern area expertise.
alternatives.concept: Study cultural encounter, migration, empire and colonialism, material and visual heritage, literature, media, museums, public rhetoric and qualitative social inquiry. Global and Mediterranean courses support analysis of representation and mobility, including a bounded encounter with Islamic courts and Arabic literary material, but the route has no Arabic acquisition, regional film/music sequence or specialist Middle Eastern cultural training.
progression: Modern history, sociology and rhetoric precede empire, cultural exchange, qualitative methodology, literature and media. Those foundations lead to advanced civil-society, museum, communication, race-and-media, art-history, literary and documentary work. No selected course has an unmet formal prerequisite, every exact planned term passes, PPD is in Year 1 and nine courses are at level 300.
alternatives.distinctness: Eleven courses / 82.5 EC differ in each direction. Comparative politics, international relations, law, EU politics, warfare, extremism and historical research give way to archaeology, heritage, literature, rhetoric, museums and art-history research, so culture and public representation—not institutions and security—organise the second programme.

blocks: Global and comparative coverage with explicit Arabic and regional-area-study gaps
Both address modern history; UCR is global and comparative rather than a dedicated modern Middle East survey.
Both address international relations; UCR provides general theory and geopolitics rather than a regional politics course.
Both address empire and colonialism; UCR is comparative and not centred on Jews and Muslims in the Middle East.
Both address conflict and security, but UCR is comparative and lacks the target’s regional case sequence.
Both can address migration and public life across Europe, but UCR is a general civil-society course rather than Middle East–Europe area study.
Both develop analysis of public persuasion and writing, but UCR is not specialist journalism about the Middle East.
Both examine cultural representation and power; UCR centres race and media rather than Middle Eastern soft power.

selection.assessment: The closest complete response is a global and comparative programme in modern history, politics, international relations, conflict and Middle East–Europe questions. A second, materially distinct route uses the separately evidenced culture, migration and artistic-representation interests to organise a coherent humanities and social-science programme. Arabic language and regional immersion were assessed next but are not feasible because UCR offers no Arabic sequence and no embedded Cairo/Rabat semester. Religion and diversity in the Middle East were assessed separately: UCR has bounded encounters with Islamic courts and Arabic literature plus general philosophy, sociology and heritage, but no Islam, Judaism, intercommunal-relations or religion-specific methods sequence. Production therefore stops at two.

notes.text: Groningen Middle Eastern Studies combines progressive Arabic, modern Middle Eastern history and politics, Judaism and Islam, culture and soft power, conflict, Europe–Middle East relations and a standard regional study period. UCR can build coherent global/comparative politics-history and culture-migration programmes, but neither is a full Middle Eastern Studies substitute.

The UCR alternatives have no Arabic acquisition, specialist Islam/Judaism study, continuous Middle Eastern regional sequence, standard Cairo/Rabat semester or scheduled Middle Eastern Studies thesis. Their limited Mediterranean and Arabic-cultural encounters are identified narrowly and are not presented as regional expertise.

The 2026–2027 curriculum contains a 30-EC Study Abroad Programme. The current official programme page describes study abroad as recommended and permits exceptional deviation, so this record preserves the component without repeating the historical judgment’s stronger claim that every student must complete it without exception.
